evals.prompt: I'm in <repo>. Show me how the whole loop actually works end to end, and give me an overview of the agents we have — what each is good at and when I should use it.
evals.expected_output: A published page: one tick in actor lanes with file:line under every stage and every exit drawn, gaps rendered as labelled gaps; a card per agent with class, model, good-at, abilities with costs, four derived stats, summon-when, weakness and hands-off-to, plus the observed Seen line; cards for the main actor, undefined-but-summoned types and vacancies; deck ordered by observed summons; bullets naming only what is visible.
assertions: Every stage in the table carries a file:line or a located absence
Stages with no evidence are drawn as labelled gaps, not omitted
Every card states class, what it is good at, abilities with costs, and a weakness
Stats that cannot be derived print an em dash rather than a number
A card exists for the main actor
A card exists for any subagent type the runs summoned that no file defines
A vacancy card exists for any class with no agent
The deck is ordered by observed summons
Counts on the cards reconcile with the window totals
The static frame carries every label and value; animation adds only sequence
Bullets each name something visible in the diagram or the deck

evals.prompt: Draw me the loop in <repo>. We have no agent files at all — it's just one session doing everything on a cron.
evals.expected_output: A flow with the single actor named on every stage, one card for the main actor, vacancy cards for the classes nobody fills, and no invented crew.
assertions: Draws the flow with the single actor named on each stage
Produces a main-actor card rather than an empty deck
Shows vacancies for the unfilled classes
Invents no agents that do not exist
Says once that no transcripts or definitions were available, rather than on every card
